title: SIMULTANEOUS OPTIMIZATION OF OFFICE BUILDING FACADES IN TERMS OF BOTH ENERGY CONSUMPTION AND TRANSPARENCY IN HOT ARID CLIMATES, ANALYSED ON THE EXAMPLE OF CAIRO
central_proposition: A scientific methodology is proposed to simultaneously optimize office facade configurations in hot-arid climates for both energy consumption and transparency, using an Energy-Transparency Balancing Factor (ETBF) to compare optimized designs.

concept_definitions.name: Transparency
concept_definitions.definition: provides crucial psychological values and benefits to the occupants. It affects their comfort, sense of well-being, and affords them view and natural light.

concept_definitions.name: Energy-Transparency Balancing Factor (ETBF)
concept_definitions.definition: the ratio of the energetically and visually optimized façade configuration preference to a virtual point that affords the maximum visual measure with the minimum energy consumption value.

concept_definitions.name: View Index
concept_definitions.definition: the measure to the ratio of the accessible visual contact to the outside, defined as “the fraction of area available as view resulting from multiplying the window-wall area, the visible transmittance of the glass, the fraction of window area not obstructed by permanent exterior shading devices, and the percentage time that interior shades do not obstruct view, times a factor near 1 that corrects for excessive reflectance from the window as seen by the occupant”.

concept_definitions.name: Psychological Comfort
concept_definitions.definition: Determined from linking the environmental design and management of the workplace with the occupant’s feelings of satisfaction, belonging, ownership, privacy and control over the workplace.

concept_definitions.name: Thermal Comfort
concept_definitions.definition: That state of mind which expresses satisfaction with the thermal environment.

concept_definitions.name: Visual Comfort
concept_definitions.definition: describes the human visual well-being and the absence of any visual discomfort in any given environment.

concept_definitions.name: Solar Protection
concept_definitions.definition: one of the most important energy efficient strategies; since almost all buildings encounters from some overheating periods in summer, and the usual response for this issue is to intervene with the energy-consuming air conditioners.

argument_structure: The paper identifies a conflict between the psychological need for transparency and the energy demands of highly glazed office buildings in hot-arid climates. It then proposes a multi-stage methodology involving contextual climate analysis, occupant surveys for psychological preferences, and energetic modeling/simulation of facade parameters. This methodology culminates in an optimization process that balances these conflicting demands, introducing a novel metric (ETBF) to evaluate the trade-offs.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: Facade design parameters (window-to-wall ratio, external shading devices, and glazed solar control concepts) directly influence both the building's energetic performance (cooling, heating, lighting loads) and the occupants' visual experience (view index, daylighting, glare, privacy). These visual experiences, in turn, impact psychological satisfaction, well-being, and productivity by regulating physiological processes (e.g., hormones, attention). The proposed methodology aims to identify optimal facade configurations by balancing these energetic and psychological outcomes based on empirically derived occupant preferences, thereby mitigating the negative 'greenhouse effect' while preserving transparency benefits.

findings.antecedent: psychological quest for high levels of office space transparency in hot-arid climates with intensive solar radiation
findings.mechanism: Glazing's poor thermal performance and selective radiation permeability (greenhouse effect) in hot-arid climates leads to excessive heat gain, necessitating high energy input for cooling.
findings.quote: the psychological quest for high levels of office space transparency in hot-arid climates with its intensive solar radiation subsequently conflict with the accompanying high rates of energy consumption.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Observed situation in Cairo, literature on glazing thermal performance.

findings.consequent: occupant comfort, sense of well-being, view, natural light, visual amenity, access to environmental information, relief from claustrophobia and monotony, recovery from daily stress, improved mood, cognition, productivity, healthy environment, reduced lighting energy, improved indoor environmental quality
findings.mechanism: Visual access to the external environment and natural light exposure regulate human biological clocks, influence hormone production (cortisol, melatonin, serotonin), reduce directed attention fatigue, and provide cognitive stimulation and restoration.
findings.quote: transparency provides crucial psychological values and benefits to the occupants. It affects their comfort, sense of well-being, and affords them view and natural light.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Literature review on psychological values of transparency (Chapter IV).

findings.antecedent: appropriate conceptual design of office building with a high degree of transparency
findings.consequent: adequate balance between transparency for psychological satisfaction/well-being and reduced total energy consumption via solar protection
findings.mechanism: A scientific methodology involving parametric analysis of facade configurations (WWR, shading, glazing) against energetic performance and visual quality (view index), guided by occupant preference ratios, allows for identifying design solutions that reconcile conflicting demands.
findings.quote: the appropriate conceptual design of office building with a high degree of transparency should take into consideration the adequate balance between two critical and at the same time conflicting requirements or tasks
findings.empirical_support_cited: The research methodology itself is the proposed solution.

findings.mechanism: ETBF quantifies the trade-off by comparing energetically and visually optimized facade preferences to a virtual ideal point (maximum visual measure, minimum energy consumption), allowing for a single metric to rank design alternatives.
findings.quote: The research proposes an Energy-Transparency Balancing Factor (ETBF) in order to compare and differentiate between the findings of these optimized configurations.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Proposed as a novel metric within the research.

findings.antecedent: occupants’ preference ratio (50% visual preference to 50% energy efficiency)
findings.consequent: required balance between visual measure (view index) and total annual energetic consumption
findings.mechanism: Empirically derived occupant preferences serve as the target balancing ratio for the optimization process, ensuring that design solutions align with human psychological needs and comfort expectations.
findings.quote: The optimization balancing ratio was concluded from the research survey findings; which is 50% preference to the visual contact to the outside and 50% preference to energy efficiency.

findings.antecedent: solar protection of the glazed components of the facades (in Cairo's climate)
findings.mechanism: By reducing solar heat gain, solar protection directly mitigates overheating, which is the most influential passive potential for improving thermal comfort in hot-arid climates.
findings.quote: the solar protection of the glazed components of the facades is the most influential passive strategy. It gives the potential to increase the internal comfortable hours with an extra 1688 hours representing 38.5% of the total occupancy hours.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Building Bio-Climatic Chart (BBCC) analysis for Cairo.

findings.consequent: total annual energy consumption values (for highly-glazed office facades in hot-arid climates)
findings.mechanism: The perforated design of Mashrabiya effectively controls sun penetration and reduces solar heat gain, making it the most energy-efficient shading device for these climates.
findings.quote: The Mashrabiya shadings are a kind of perforated shading devices that were traditionally introduced and developed for the hot-arid climates in the MENA area... These shadings evidently showed that they are the most energy efficient shading devices for the highly-glazed office facades in hot-arid climates.

findings.consequent: lowest total annual energy consumption values AND highest optimized view index measures
findings.mechanism: Advanced solar control properties of triple glazing (low light transmittance, high SHGC) allow for larger window-to-wall ratios to meet transparency targets while maintaining energy efficiency.
findings.quote: glazing concept G3 (triple glazing) always achieved the lowest total annual energy consumption values... it achieved the highest optimized view index measures, since it requires higher window to wall ratio to meet with the optimizing axe

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: The proposed methodology can be developed into a computer software to assist architects in designing energy-efficient and psychologically satisfying office facades.
The methodology can be applied to other hot and sunny cities/countries to examine cultural preferences for transparency.
Different movable shading devices and advanced solar control concepts (automated, switchable glazing) can be integrated and examined within the research methodology.
Optimizing perforated shadings (Mashrabiya) with different types, patterns, solar shading angles, and materials can increase visual measure while preserving energetic performance.
The methodology can be applied to other building types (residential, medical, educational), considering specific psychological factors like privacy for residential buildings.

Other visual measures (glare index, daylight factor) and energy-efficient concepts (natural ventilation, evaporative cooling, photovoltaics) can be investigated and integrated within the research methodology.
bridge_warrants: The methodology integrates engineering principles of energy efficiency with psychological principles of human well-being and satisfaction.
It combines climatic analysis, occupant preference surveys, and building energy simulations to create a holistic design approach.
The Energy-Transparency Balancing Factor (ETBF) serves as a novel metric to bridge and quantify the trade-offs between energy consumption and visual transparency.
methodological_critiques: Current commercial buildings in hot-arid climates are often based on international models maladapted to local climatic conditions, leading to high energy consumption.
A narrow focus solely on energy conservation in building design can lead to windowless designs that neglect occupants' psychological needs for external views and daylighting.

Unoptimized glazed office buildings in Cairo lead to intensive solar radiation transmittance, causing occupants to close internal shadings, which deprives them of transparency and increases energy consumption for cooling and lighting.
model_structure: The research operational study (Figure 1-9, p. 45) outlines a four-pillar process: 1) Cairo Contextual Study (climate, energy stats, building consumption patterns) to inform solar protective strategies (shading, glazing, WWR); 2) Surveying Psychological Preference to Transparency (importance, interaction, preferred design criteria); 3) Energetic Modeling and Simulation (comparing typical Egyptian vs. ASHRAE profiles, then simulating solar protection parameters); and 4) Optimizing Energy Efficiency with Transparency using a 'View Index' and the proposed Energy-Transparency Balancing Factor (ETBF).
limitations: The current research is limited to the context of Cairo and needs to be examined in other hot and sunny cities/countries to understand cultural preferences for transparency.
The study examined a specific set of fixed external shading devices and glazing concepts; future work could integrate different movable shading devices, automated systems, or switchable glazing.

The methodology was applied to office buildings; its applicability to other building types (residential, medical, educational) needs further investigation, considering specific psychological factors like privacy.
The visual measures used were limited to the view index; future studies could integrate other visual measures such as glare index or daylight factor.
The energy-efficient concepts investigated were limited to solar protection; future work could integrate other concepts like natural ventilation, evaporative cooling, or photovoltaics.

mechanism_chain.description: The human desire for transparent office spaces in hot climates leads to architectural designs with large glazed areas. These designs, in turn, increase solar heat gain, necessitating higher cooling loads and consequently leading to increased energy consumption.
